pr.title: List a page's sections and a nested project's neighbors in its sidebar
pr.head: 15e7583ef32b3ca00dbfec6ee6b951f9acf0852e

summary: A project page on the Projector site shows a plan beside a sidebar, drawn the way a pull request summary's sidebar is: the project's stacks of pull requests, then the project's other pages. Unlike a summary's sidebar, it has no list of the page's sections, so on a plan of 500 to 800 lines you scroll to find a section. A nested project's sidebar also has no link to its parent or to its sibling projects, so you go through the breadcrumbs.

This pull request adds both. The sidebar lists the page's ## headings, read from the page after it renders, with the plan's own number in a column of its own. A nested project's sidebar ends with its parent project over the parent's other nested projects. One helper, watchSections, marks the section in view as you scroll, on project pages and on summary pages. At 980 pixels and narrower, the list starts folded behind a Sections toggle. At the owner's request, the project page's View on GitHub link also moves into a … menu at the end of the title row, the same menu a summary page's header has. A jump to a section lands its heading level with the top of the sticky sidebar, and the page leaves room after its last section so that section can scroll there too.
The build and site.json do not change: everything happens in the browser, in the TypeScript under site/src/ and its compiled copies under site/assets/.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Section: a top-level ## heading of a rendered page, or a group on a summary page.
  • Mark: aria-current="location" on the sidebar link to the section in view, drawn as a band with an accent bar.
  • The line: a horizontal line 30% of the way down the window. The marked section is the last one whose top has passed it.
  • Neighbors: a nested project's parent and the parent's other nested projects.

cards.title: Review status
cards.html: The first Projector review, of b676859, flagged that a jump carrying a heading past the line in one frame was never reported. The fix extends the observer's band far above the page and was confirmed at fd7e766. The author then held the pull request for two changes: land a jumped-to heading level with the sidebar, and leave room after the last section. The review of 15e7583 checked both in headless Chrome and is clean.

groups.title: The shared section list and the watch
groups.kicker: Helpers that summary pages and project pages both use
intro: summary.ts holds helpers that every site page loads before site.js. This group adds two of them. sectionListHtml draws a list of sections, with the summary's reviewed dots or without them. watchSections marks the link to the section in view and keeps the mark current as the page scrolls. It also moves moreMenu and wireMenus, the summary page's … menu, out of the summary page's own code into the shared helpers, so that project pages can use them.

The watch uses one IntersectionObserver and no scroll listener. It watches each section's target against a band that runs from far above the page down to a line 30% of the way down the window, so a target is in the band exactly while its top is above the line. Each report reads every target's position again and moves the mark. Because the page leaves room after its last section, every section can reach the line by scrolling, and the watch needs no rule of its own for the end of the page.

files.note: Adds PageSection, a section's id, number, and title, and MenuItem, one link in a … menu.
Adds sectionListHtml and watchSections, and moves moreMenu and wireMenus to the shared helpers unchanged.

checks.text: A jump that carries a heading past the line in one frame moves the mark. In headless Chrome 151, with the compiled watchSections, a scrollTo into the middle of a long section marked it, and a jump back to the top cleared the mark.
The summary's list is the markup it drew before, plus class="sections" on the <ol>; SectionWatchTests asserts the exact markup, and the suite passes at this head.

files.note: Draws the mark, lands a jump's target 16 pixels below the sticky offset, level with the sidebar, and gives a page's last section room to scroll there.

checks.text: In headless Chrome at 1,200 by 857 pixels, a click on the last section of incremental-review landed its heading at 16 pixels, level with the sidebar's top, and marked it.

groups.title: The project page sidebar
groups.kicker: Sections, a nested project's neighbors, the narrow-screen toggle, and the title row's menu
intro: A project page draws its sidebar twice: once while the Markdown loads, and again once it renders. showDocument now passes the sidebar as a function of the page's sections, so the second drawing can list the headings the render produced, with the ids the render gave them. An HTML page lists no sections.

projectNav puts the readme's sections in their own block between the stacks and the pages. On a supplemental page, the sections open under that page's entry in the pages, through a new under argument to tree. A nested project's sidebar then ends with its neighbors, found by parentOf, the deepest project whose folder holds the nested project's folder.

The title row's View on GitHub link becomes a … menu with View file on GitHub and View history on GitHub. frame wires the menus of each drawing, and an HTML page wires the menu in the breadcrumbs it adds after frame runs.

On a page with a title row, showDocument moves the last ## heading and everything after it into one lastsection element. A plan's sections are not elements of their own, so this wrapper is what the CSS can give a minimum height, leaving room for the last section to scroll to the top.

checks.text: frame stops the watch before it draws any view, and showDocument starts it again after the render, so only one list is watched at a time.

files.note: Reads the rendered sections, draws the new sidebar blocks and the title row's menu, and flips the Sections toggle.

checks.text: sectionOf moves a leading number such as 2. or 2.1 to the number column, and keeps a year such as 2026 roadmap in the title. Links are removed by unwrapping them in a copy of the heading. sectionHeadings takes only top-level <h2> elements, so a heading inside a quote is not listed.

The wrapper changes no rendering: every Markdown style in site.css uses a descendant selector, such as .markdown h2, and the heading's top margin collapses through the wrapper. In headless Chrome a jump to the last heading landed it inside lastsection at 16 pixels.

parentOf drops the folder's trailing slash before it calls ownerOf, so the project never finds itself. The nested-project tests in ProjectPageTests pass, including a nested project of the current one that stays out of the neighbors.
Each menu gets its listeners once: frame wires what it draws, and this call wires only the head appended after it. Traced through frame, showHtml, and showDocument.

files.note: Dividers for the new blocks, a two-column row for a plan's sections, the toggle that folds them at 980 pixels and narrower, an HTML page's breadcrumbs row with the menu at its end, and a sticky offset of 0 on a narrow project page, which has no compact bar.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: Page, watch, and style tests under node
intro: The page tests run the compiled showProjectFile under node with a stub DOM. The watch tests run watchSections with a stub IntersectionObserver and call its callbacks directly, so they check the marking rule but not which scrolls the browser reports.

groups.title: The plan and the CLI docs
groups.kicker: The settled plan, marked completed, and the site description
intro: The plan project-page-sections records each question, its options, and the owner's decision, then the sidebar those decisions make. It ends completed, with an outcome section that lists the browser checks and the menu change the owner added. docs/cli.md describes the new sidebar and the menu.

checks.text: § 2.10 gives the observer's band as 10000000px 0px -70% 0px, and § 7 records the owner's two later requests: a jump lands level with the sidebar, and the last section gets room to scroll there.
